source: Aswath Damodaran, valuation packet 2 (spring 2021 and spring 2020 editions), NYU Stern. Regional multiple regressions, the US market-wide PE and PEG regressions, the country PE regression, the US grocery sector price-to-sales fits, the early-2000 internet price-to-sales fit, and the S&P 500 earnings-yield regression.
refresh: https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/ — 'Multiples by region' and the annual data update. Coefficients move sharply year to year: the US price of an extra percentage point of expected growth ranged from 0.41 (Jan 2012) to 2.62 (Jan 2003) over two decades. Re-estimate every period rather than reusing a stale fit, and record which vintage a valuation used.
units_warning: Unless an entry says otherwise, every predictor enters as a decimal: 25% growth is 0.25, a 30% payout is 0.30, a 20% margin is 0.20. Two entries (us_peg_jan2021 and us_pe_2019_through_origin) reproduce SPSS output in which payout and growth are absolute percentages; their units field says so.

us_pe_jan2021.description: US trailing PE on payout and expected EPS growth, weighted least squares by market cap, after dropping the insignificant beta. This is the form used for firm-level application.
us_pe_jan2021.definition: payout = dividends / net income in the most recent year, set to zero if net income is negative; growth = consensus expected EPS growth over the next five years
cautions: The growth coefficient is the market price of an extra percentage point of expected growth. At 2.28 (decimal scale) January 2021 was the second-richest reading in two decades.
Beta was dropped because its t-statistic was 0.633. Dropping it moved R-squared only from 0.396 to 0.389.

us_pe_jan2021_with_beta.description: The same US regression before the insignificant beta was dropped.
us_pe_jan2021_with_beta.units: payout and growth as decimals, beta as a plain number
us_pe_jan2021_with_beta.definition: as us_pe_jan2021, with beta = regression or bottom-up beta
cautions: Beta's t-statistic is 0.633, so its coefficient carries no information.

us_pe_2019_through_origin.description: The negative-intercept fix: the 2019 US PE regression re-run through the origin so no firm gets a negative predicted multiple.
us_pe_2019_through_origin.units: payout and growth in absolute percentage points (25% enters as 25)
us_pe_2019_through_origin.definition: as us_pe_jan2021, in percent units and with no intercept
cautions: Fitting through the origin is an imperfect fix. It removes negative predictions at the cost of forcing the line through a point no firm occupies.

europe_pe_jan2021.description: European PE on beta, payout and expected EPS growth.
europe_pe_jan2021.definition: beta, payout, five-year expected EPS growth

japan_pe_jan2021.description: Japanese PE on beta, payout and expected EPS growth.
japan_pe_jan2021.definition: beta, payout, five-year expected EPS growth

em_pe_jan2021.description: Emerging-market PE on beta, payout and expected EPS growth.
em_pe_jan2021.definition: beta, payout, five-year expected EPS growth

anzc_pe_jan2021.description: Australia, New Zealand and Canada PE on beta, payout and expected EPS growth.
anzc_pe_jan2021.definition: beta, payout, five-year expected EPS growth

global_pe_jan2021.description: Global PE on beta, payout and expected EPS growth.
global_pe_jan2021.definition: beta, payout, five-year expected EPS growth

us_peg_jan2021.description: US PEG on payout, the log of expected growth, and beta. The log transform is the standard fix for the non-linear PEG-growth relationship: R-squared on raw growth is 0.022 against 0.053 on ln(growth).
us_peg_jan2021.units: payout and growth in absolute percentage points (a 25% payout enters as 25, 20% growth enters as 20 before the log is taken)
us_peg_jan2021.definition: payout = dividends / net income; growth = expected EPS growth over the next five years; beta = regression or bottom-up beta
cautions: R-squared of 0.116 means fundamentals explain far less of PEG than of PE. Hold any conclusion loosely.
The regional PEG table in the same packet states payout and growth as decimals while this SPSS output states them as percentages. Check which convention a coefficient set uses before applying it.
PEG falls with beta and with the level of growth, so a low PEG often marks the riskiest or fastest-growing firm rather than the cheapest.

us_pbv_jan2021.description: US price-to-book on beta, payout, expected EPS growth and ROE.
us_pbv_jan2021.definition: roe = net income / book value of equity, most recent year

europe_pbv_jan2021.description: European price-to-book on beta, payout, expected EPS growth and ROE.
europe_pbv_jan2021.definition: roe = net income / book value of equity

japan_pbv_jan2021.description: Japanese price-to-book on beta, payout, expected EPS growth and ROE.
japan_pbv_jan2021.definition: roe = net income / book value of equity
cautions: The positive beta coefficient is a multicollinearity artefact, not a finding that risk raises price-to-book in Japan.

em_pbv_jan2021.description: Emerging-market price-to-book on beta, payout, expected EPS growth and ROE.
em_pbv_jan2021.definition: roe = net income / book value of equity
cautions: The intercept is negative, so a firm with weak fundamentals can be handed a negative predicted price-to-book. Refuse that prediction rather than reporting it.

anzc_pbv_jan2021.description: Australia, New Zealand and Canada price-to-book on beta, payout, expected EPS growth and ROE.
anzc_pbv_jan2021.definition: roe = net income / book value of equity

global_pbv_jan2021.description: Global price-to-book on beta, payout, expected EPS growth and ROE.
global_pbv_jan2021.definition: roe = net income / book value of equity

us_ev_ebitda_jan2021.description: US EV/EBITDA on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and the effective tax rate.
us_ev_ebitda_jan2021.definition: debt_ratio = total debt / (total debt + market value of equity); revenue_growth = expected near-term revenue growth; tax_rate = effective tax rate in the most recent year

europe_ev_ebitda_jan2021.description: European EV/EBITDA on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and the effective tax rate.

japan_ev_ebitda_jan2021.description: Japanese EV/EBITDA on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and the effective tax rate.
cautions: R-squared of 10.3% and a wrong-signed debt-ratio coefficient. Treat any prediction from this fit as illustrative.

em_ev_ebitda_jan2021.description: Emerging-market EV/EBITDA on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and the effective tax rate.

anzc_ev_ebitda_jan2021.description: Australia, New Zealand and Canada EV/EBITDA on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and the effective tax rate.
cautions: Weak fit; the prediction is weak evidence.

global_ev_ebitda_jan2021.description: Global EV/EBITDA on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and the effective tax rate.

us_ev_sales_jan2021.description: US EV/Sales on the effective tax rate, debt ratio, expected revenue growth and operating margin. Slide labelled January 2020, carried in the 2021 packet.
us_ev_sales_jan2021.definition: operating_margin = operating income / sales; the rest as in us_ev_ebitda_jan2021

europe_ev_sales_jan2021.description: European EV/Sales on the effective tax rate, debt ratio, expected revenue growth and operating margin.
cautions: Weak fit; the tax and debt-ratio signs both invert relative to theory.

japan_ev_sales_jan2021.description: Japanese EV/Sales on the effective tax rate, debt ratio, expected revenue growth and operating margin.

em_ev_sales_jan2021.description: Emerging-market EV/Sales on the effective tax rate, debt ratio, expected revenue growth and operating margin.

anzc_ev_sales_jan2021.description: Australia, New Zealand and Canada EV/Sales on the effective tax rate, debt ratio, expected revenue growth and operating margin.

global_ev_sales_jan2021.description: Global EV/Sales on the effective tax rate, debt ratio, expected revenue growth and operating margin.
cautions: The operating-margin coefficient sits between 5.4 and 7.9 in every region. Margin is the dominant companion variable everywhere.

us_ev_ic_jan2021.description: US EV/Invested Capital on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and ROIC. Slide labelled January 2020, carried in the 2021 packet.
us_ev_ic_jan2021.definition: roic = after-tax return on invested capital; invested capital = book equity + book debt - cash
cautions: EV/IC regressions have the tightest fit of any multiple family. When multiples disagree, weight this one more heavily.

europe_ev_ic_jan2021.description: European EV/Invested Capital on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and ROIC.

japan_ev_ic_jan2021.description: Japanese EV/Invested Capital on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and ROIC.

em_ev_ic_jan2021.description: Emerging-market EV/Invested Capital on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and ROIC.

anzc_ev_ic_jan2021.description: Australia, New Zealand and Canada EV/Invested Capital on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and ROIC.

global_ev_ic_jan2021.description: Global EV/Invested Capital on the debt ratio, expected revenue growth and ROIC.

country_pe_2000.description: Country PE on the local interest rate, expected real GDP growth and a country risk score. Estimated on 16 emerging markets, June 2000.
country_pe_2000.units: interest_rate and real_gdp_growth as decimals; country_risk on a 0-100 scale where higher is riskier
country_pe_2000.definition: interest_rate = long-term local rate; real_gdp_growth = expected real GDP growth; country_risk = composite risk score on the scale the regression was fitted on
cautions: The risk coefficient is scale-specific. A score on a different scale gives a meaningless prediction.
Sixteen observations with three predictors is thin. Rates and risk premia have moved enormously since June 2000; refit before use.

us_grocery_ps_2007.description: US grocery sector price-to-sales on the net margin, January 2007.

us_grocery_ps_2010.description: US grocery sector price-to-sales on the net margin, January 2010.

us_grocery_ps_2015.description: US grocery sector price-to-sales on the net margin, January 2015.
cautions: The fit collapsed from 0.595 in 2007 to 0.291 in 2015 while the coefficients moved in every vintage. Sector regressions are not stable; re-estimate.

internet_ps_2000.description: Early-2000 internet stocks: price-to-sales on survival and growth proxies, used because every firm in the sector had a negative margin. Regressing on the current margin gave R-squared of 0.04.
internet_ps_2000.units: ln_revenue = natural log of revenues, already logged by the caller; revenue_growth and cash_over_revenue as decimals
internet_ps_2000.definition: ln_revenue is a size control; cash_over_revenue is the survival proxy
cautions: A relative verdict inside a bubble is still relative. Every firm in this sample was priced against peers who were collectively overpriced.

sp500_earnings_yield_1960_2020.description: S&P 500 earnings yield on the ten-year Treasury rate and the bond-bill spread, 1960-2020. Invert the predicted yield to get a predicted market PE.
sp500_earnings_yield_1960_2020.definition: tbond_rate = ten-year Treasury rate; bond_bill_spread = ten-year rate minus the short-term Treasury rate
cautions: The output is an earnings yield, not a multiple. Invert it: predicted market PE = 1 / predicted E/P.
The relationship weakened after 2008. Fitted through 2008 the same regression had R-squared of 0.5071 and a significant spread term; through 2020 the spread term is insignificant.
